original_question: If a bipartite graph G has bipartition (A, B), maximum degree Delta_A on side A, and maximum degree Delta_B on side B, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta_A Delta_B?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Conjecture 27: the Brualdi–Quinn conjecture. In the survey’s exact formulation, if G is bipartite with parts A and B, then χ_s(G) ≤ Δ_AΔ_B, where Δ_A and Δ_B are the maximum degrees, respectively, of vertices in A and B. The same problem is restated in Section 6 as open problem 7. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right graph class (bipartite graphs), the right partition data (A,B), the right side-specific degree parameters (Δ_A and Δ_B), and the exact inequality from the paper’s official statement. It is aiming at the strengthened Brualdi–Quinn conjecture, not the earlier broader predecessor χ_s(G) ≤ Δ^2 for bipartite graphs. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define χ_s(G) as the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

It should define a strong edge-coloring explicitly: two edges must receive distinct colors whenever they share an endpoint, or whenever they each share an endpoint with the same edge. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

It should make the universal quantifier explicit: the statement is intended to hold for every bipartite graph G with parts A and B. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

It should specify the degree parameters as Δ_A := max{d_G(a) : a ∈ A} and Δ_B := max{d_G(b) : b ∈ B}, matching the paper’s wording that these are the maximum degrees of vertices in A and B, respectively. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
refined_question: Is the following Brualdi–Quinn conjecture true: for every bipartite graph G with parts A and B, if χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of G such that any two edges that share an endpoint, or that each share an endpoint with a common edge, receive distinct colors, and if Δ_A := max{d_G(a) : a ∈ A} and Δ_B := max{d_G(b) : b ∈ B}, then must χ_s(G) satisfy χ_s(G) ≤ Δ_AΔ_B? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since a strong edge-coloring of G is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph L(G), is it true that every bipartite graph G with parts A and B satisfies χ(L(G)^2) ≤ Δ_AΔ_B, where Δ_A and Δ_B are the maximum degrees on the two parts? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s intended statement. In Section 4.1, the survey first mentions the earlier conjecture χ_s(G) ≤ Δ^2 for bipartite graphs and then immediately states the stronger asymmetric version as Conjecture 27, which is exactly what your use of Δ_A and Δ_B is trying to capture. The surrounding context on pp. 17–18 gives the precise meaning of strong edge-coloring and χ_s(G), and Section 6 confirms this identification by restating the same problem as open problem 7. So the only substantive refinements needed are the formal definition of χ_s(G), the explicit strong-coloring condition, and explicit definitions of Δ_A and Δ_B. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
